curriculum.subject: LANGUAGE_ARTS
curriculum.description: Students listen to words and interact with a visual interface to segment the word into individual syllables. Focus: Developing auditory and visual awareness of syllable counts in words. Examples: apple, tiger, rabbit, basket, tunnel, magnet, button, winter, candle, napkin. Constraints: Provide visual feedback for every correct syllable clap in the syllable-clapper primitive.

status: authored; catalog-checked; each binding generator-probed once; not hydrated as a lesson; not runtime-tested
learnerAction: Hear a word and clap and count its syllables (1-3), then say the parts.

components.title: Put the Parts Together
components.intent: Grade 2 picturable words of 1-3 syllables; the tutor says the parts, the child says the word.

components.title: Clap and Count
components.intent: Grade 2 picturable words; MIX 1-, 2- and 3-syllable words so the count changes from word to word (cat, rabbit, banana, basket, elephant).

components.title: Count New Words
components.intent: Grade 2, fresh words, mixed 1-3 syllables; no words from the previous activity.

evidenceCriteria: Says the correct syllable count across words whose counts differ.
coverageLimits: The probe drew eight 2-syllable words copied from the curriculum examples, so "two" is always right. The generator has no code rule that spreads the counts.
The workspace lists grades K-1; the objective is grade 2 (the act is the same).

recommendation.rationale: Repair, not new: count_parts needs a code rule that a session spans at least two different counts. Route to /eval-fix (SYC-1).
